Losses are held-out losses in nats per token at the end of training. A rung of the ladder is the mean of its two seeds; a put-back into the 2026 recipe is the mean over the seeds that have run, each against the recipe of the same seed; the warmup runs are one seed each. Two yardsticks. The ladder's (it serves for the ladder and for anything trained with AdamW): the two seeds of a rung differ by 0.001 to 0.018 nats over the 10 rungs of the ladder: 0.006 or less on 8 of them, 0.015 on RMS norm without parameters and 0.018 on the 2019 recipe; root mean square 0.008; under 0.016 between two single runs is noise. Numbers are rounded to six significant digits first, as in the files the figures read.

results_lines.Section 5.2, where the norm sits: whethe: No. At initialization post-norm is level, not rising: under GPT-2's initialization every block but the first receives the same gradient (0.079 at 48 blocks; the first, which reads the raw embedding, 0.94), and with Glorot weights the two ends differ by at most 23% and in no steady direction (1.35 to 1.58 at 12 blocks, 1.41 to 1.53 at 24 blocks, 1.99 to 1.53 at 48 blocks). Pre-norm is the one with a slope, and it falls toward the output: 3.59 to 1.25 at 48 blocks under GPT-2's initialization, 1.31 to 0.27 with Glorot weights, as its stream grows (1.14 to 6.62). The top-layer gradient with depth agrees with Proposition 5.2.5 in its own setting (Glorot weights): from 12 to 48 blocks it changes by a factor 0.94 for post-norm and 0.47 for pre-norm (1/sqrt(4) = 0.50); under GPT-2's initialization, whose 1/sqrt(2L) makes the pre-norm stream end at the same size at every depth (0.088, 0.088, 0.088), it does not change in either (1.00, 1.01). Training at 8 layers, the 2019 recipe, 50M tokens, one seed each, in steps of 8,192 tokens at rate 0.0006 (the warmup of 8M tokens is 977 steps): pre-norm 4.581 with a warmup and 4.950 without; post-norm 4.537 with a warmup and 7.696 without. With a warmup post-norm trains and is 0.044 ahead; without one it collapses to token frequencies (for scale, token frequencies alone give 7.70 on held-out text (the unigram level of part 8's replayed run) and a uniform guess over the 32,768 tokens 10.40) where pre-norm loses 0.37. At the ladder's step of 65,536 tokens and rate 0.0024, where the same warmup is 122 steps, post-norm collapsed to token frequencies with a warmup too (7.690, 7.690), within 40 steps and pre-norm reached 4.613 and 5.706: those two post-norm runs are a collapse, not evidence about warmup, and nothing here says that post-norm cannot train. With a warmup of 32M tokens (488 steps) post-norm at that step still collapses at rate 0.0024 (7.691) and trains at rate 0.0006, to 5.255 (pre-norm at that step: 4.613): at the large step it takes both a long warmup and a low rate, and it ends far behind. In the 2026 recipe (Muon, writers at zero, 50M tokens) post-norm trains too: 4.133 against 4.026 for the same layer norm placed before the sublayers.
results_lines.Section 5.2, which norm: whether layer n: Layer norm (4.026) and RMS norm with a gain (4.025) are within 0.001 of each other in seed 0 and the same in the mean of two seeds: centering does not matter. Both are better than the parameter-free RMS norm of the recipe (4.045): layer norm −0.020 (−0.019 and −0.021 in two seeds; better in both seeds), RMS norm with a gain −0.020 (−0.020 and −0.021 in two seeds; better in both seeds). The second seed repeats the first: the learned gain is worth about 0.02 nats at this size. On the ladder, where a rung is the mean of two seeds, the same step (rung 3, layer norm with its gain to parameter-free RMS norm) cost +0.031 (+0.026 in one seed, +0.037 in the other). Dynamic tanh lands at 4.077, +0.031 (one seed; worse); dynamic tanh was run at 3 slopes (0.25: +0.035, 0.5: +0.031, 1: +0.044); the default was the best. Without normalization the model does not train even with zero-initialized projections: the loss was 5.98 at step 70 and not finite at step 80.
results_lines.Section 5.3, the activations: the order: Lowest to highest loss in seed 0: SwiGLU 4.037, GeGLU 4.043, squared ReLU 4.045, GELU 4.046, SiLU 4.052, ReLU 4.063. Against squared ReLU, each seed against the recipe of the same seed (under 0.009 is noise under this recipe): SwiGLU −0.009 (−0.008 and −0.011 in two seeds; inside seed noise); GeGLU −0.002 (one seed; inside seed noise); GELU −0.001 (+0.001 and −0.002 in two seeds; inside seed noise); SiLU +0.007 (+0.007 and +0.006 in two seeds; inside seed noise); ReLU +0.017 (+0.018 and +0.016 in two seeds; worse in both seeds). The second-order units average 4.042 and the first-order ones 4.054 in seed 0: 0.012 apart, mostly ReLU's doing; GELU ties squared ReLU. The 0.02 to 0.05 of the literature is there against ReLU only, at 8 layers and 50M tokens. What differs more is what the units do: 83% of squared ReLU's activations and 86% of ReLU's are exact zeros, GELU has 1%; the kurtosis of the activations is 1306 for squared ReLU, 289 and 306 for the two gated units and 43 for GELU; dead units are rare in all six: none in 5 of them and 0.03% of the units at most (relu2).
results_lines.Section 5.4, neurons as memories: whethe: In part. The share of a neuron's 25 strongest triggers that end in its commonest last token is highest in block 2 (0.41) and lowest in block 12 (0.26); random positions give 0.08. Lower layers are the more shallow, as in the 2021 table, but by a modest margin. The top token of a value is the token after its key's strongest trigger for 1% of the neurons of block 1, 13% in block 9 and 5% in block 12 (chance 0.003%): values continue their triggers in the upper half, not at the very top. Coefficients are non-negative (squared ReLU). 200 neurons sampled a block, the 25 strongest triggers of each.
results_lines.Section 5.5, the initializations: whethe: Only two of the three were run. With the writers scaled by 1/sqrt(2L) the 2026 recipe ends at 4.0438, with the writers at zero at 4.0451: 0.0013 apart, inside seed noise. During training the two cross: −0.010 at 10M tokens, +0.010 at 20M tokens (scaled less zero). No difference at the end and none that lasts early, at 8 layers. Plain 0.02 on every matrix was not run, so the sources' claim that the scaled rule clearly beats it is untested here. On the ladder, under AdamW at 100M tokens, zero writers were −0.027 against the scaled rule (−0.025 in one seed, −0.030 in the other); with a warmup of 32M tokens that step shrinks to −0.008 (seed 0).
results_lines.Section 5.6, the table: the swaps that c: The 2026 recipe with one old part put back (50M tokens; the mean over the seeds that have run, each against the recipe of the same seed; under 0.009 is noise under this recipe). The rows of the post's table that cost the most: learned positions +0.110, no query-key normalization +0.031. Every swap run, by standing (two numbers in brackets: the two seeds). Established, the old part costs: pos-none +0.264, sched-constant +0.150, pos-sinusoidal +0.133, pos-learned +0.110 (+0.112, +0.108), norm-post +0.088, pos-sinusoidal-after-norm +0.059 (+0.060, +0.058), attn-mqa +0.050, norm-dyt-a1 +0.044, norm-dyt-a0.25 +0.035, norm-dyt +0.031, sched-cosine +0.031, attn-no-qk-norm +0.031 (+0.029, +0.032), attn-gqa2 +0.030, act-relu +0.017 (+0.018, +0.016), sched-linear +0.011 (+0.011, +0.011), and without normalization the run diverged. Established, the old part is better: bias −0.017 (−0.021, −0.013), norm-layernorm −0.020 (−0.019, −0.021), norm-rmsnorm-gain −0.020 (−0.020, −0.021), bias-lrg0.03 −0.023. At the edge: no-embed-norm +0.011 (+0.014, +0.008), norm-rmsnorm-gain-lrg0.03 −0.013. Inside seed noise: act-silu +0.007 (+0.007, +0.006), attn-gqa4 +0.003, pos-alibi +0.002, attn-qk-learned +0.001, tied 0.000, act-gelu −0.001 (+0.001, −0.002), init-gpt2 −0.001, act-geglu −0.002, no-softcap −0.002, no-warmup −0.003 (−0.008, +0.002), act-swiglu −0.009 (−0.008, −0.011). The full 2019 recipe ends at 4.135 and the full 2026 recipe at 3.814 (the ladder, 100M tokens, means of two seeds): a gap of 0.321, of which the training recipe of 2026 (rung 7: Muon on the hidden matrices, with its rates and its schedule) is 0.155 (48%) and the eight changes to the block 0.165 (52%); rotary positions alone are 0.110. Rung by rung, the step of the means and of each seed: no biases 0.000 (−0.010 in one seed, +0.010 in the other), rotary positions −0.110 (−0.111 in one seed, −0.110 in the other), RMS norm without parameters +0.031 (+0.026 in one seed, +0.037 in the other), squared ReLU −0.033 (−0.022 in one seed, −0.043 in the other), QK normalization −0.011 (−0.016 in one seed, −0.007 in the other), zero-initialized writers −0.027 (−0.025 in one seed, −0.030 in the other), the training recipe of 2026 −0.155 (−0.157 in one seed, −0.154 in the other), untied tables with a normalized embedding −0.011 (−0.012 in one seed, −0.010 in the other), the soft cap −0.003 (+0.000 in one seed, −0.006 in the other). With a warmup of 32M tokens each rung trained by the 2019 recipe is 0.017 to 0.042 better (seed 0): the published 2019 rungs sit about 0.03 above what a longer warmup gives them. At 8 layers and 50M tokens two simplifications of the 2026 block do cost, in both seeds: the parameter-free norm (layer norm with its gain put back −0.020 (−0.019 and −0.021 in two seeds; better in both seeds); RMS norm with a gain −0.020 (−0.020 and −0.021 in two seeds; better in both seeds)) and the missing biases (put back −0.017 (−0.021 and −0.013 in two seeds; better in both seeds)). Squared ReLU is worth 0.017 over ReLU (+0.018 and +0.016 in two seeds) and nothing over GELU (−0.001 (+0.001 and −0.002 in two seeds; inside seed noise)). On the ladder, removing the biases is worth nothing (−0.0001 on the means: −0.010 in one seed, +0.010 in the other), and the parameter-free norm costs +0.031 (+0.026 in one seed, +0.037 in the other). Also established: rotary positions (a learned table +0.110 (+0.112 and +0.108 in two seeds; worse in both seeds)), the training recipe of 2026 (−0.155 on the ladder), query-key normalization (without it +0.031 (+0.029 and +0.032 in two seeds; worse in both seeds)) and pre-norm (+0.088 with post-norm and layer norm, +0.107 against the same layer norm before the sublayers, seed 0). The norm on the embedding: +0.011 (+0.014 and +0.008 in two seeds; worse, at the edge of seed noise) without it, 0.000 when it goes together with the second vocabulary matrix (the tied run, 16.8M parameters fewer). Under the 2026 recipe (50M tokens) two seeds of one configuration differ by 0.001 to 0.008 nats over the 14 pairs that exist (root mean square 0.005): a difference of 0.009 or more between two such runs is established. The ladder and the swaps ask different questions and twice give different answers: squared ReLU gained 0.033 on the ladder (−0.022 in one seed, −0.043 in the other; under AdamW, right after the norm lost its gain) and GELU put back into the finished recipe is −0.001 (+0.001 and −0.002 in two seeds; inside seed noise); writers at zero gained 0.027 on the ladder (−0.025 in one seed, −0.030 in the other) and the scaled rule put back is −0.001 (one seed; inside seed noise). Query-key normalization goes the other way: −0.011 on the ladder (−0.016 in one seed, −0.007 in the other), +0.031 (+0.029 and +0.032 in two seeds; worse in both seeds) when taken out of the finished recipe. Rung 7 taken apart: with AdamW in place of Muon under the 2026 training recipe the rung-6 model ends at 3.911 and 3.915 in two seeds: Muon in place of AdamW is 0.083 and 0.086, the rest of the recipe 0.074 and 0.068 against rung 6 as published; against rung 6 with a warmup of 32M tokens (3.968, seed 0) the step is 0.140, not 0.157, and the rest of the recipe 0.057.
